speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I see you are presenting with postmenopausal bleeding and an adnexal mass; to determine the cause, I need to ask you a few specific questions. How old are you, and when did your menstrual periods last occur?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old woman. The patient presents with a 2-month history of intermittent postmenopausal bleeding. She denies any recent weight loss, fever, or changes in bladder or bowel habits. No previous history of similar symptoms. She has no history of serious illness and takes no medications regularly.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the information; I will proceed as if these details are accurate. Given your age and the adnexal mass, I need to know if you have a history of hormone replacement therapy or prior breast cancer. REQUEST TEST: Serum CA-125 and Transvaginal Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound shows a thickened endometrial stripe of 12 mm, which is the most concerning finding for endometrial pathology. Given your age and the mass, have you had any difficulty urinating, such as a feeling of incomplete emptying, or have you noticed any foul-smelling vaginal discharge? REQUEST TEST: Endometrial Biopsy and Pelvic MRI.
